cohort: The study included pregnant women with a healthy, single pregnancy between 37-40 weeks gestation, who experienced either an uncomplicated vaginal birth (n=33) or an elective caesarean section delivery (n=26).
finding: Delivery mode influences oxidative stress markers and antioxidant enzyme activity, with vaginal delivery associated with higher oxidative stress in maternal and cord blood, and cesarean section delivery associated with higher oxidative stress marker levels in maternal milk.
mod_finding: Vaginal delivery was associated with higher oxidative stress (GPX, CAT, MDA levels) in maternal serum and umbilical cord blood, while cesarean section delivery was associated with higher oxidative stress (MDA levels) in maternal milk.
